accuracy.evidence: The placement matches Development Matters (2021) PSED for 3 and 4 year olds (find solutions to conflicts and rivalries; begin to understand how others might be feeling) and the EYFS ELGs Building Relationships (work and play cooperatively and take turns) and Managing Self (know right from wrong and try to behave accordingly); the routine (ask, accept the answer, care for it, return it, own up to damage) follows PSHE Association KS1 guidance on respecting others' belongings. The logic was checked by hand: Mia lends, Sam's not-now and Leo's no each accept only the kind reply; the straight route meets a hazard and the edge route clears every hazard by more than its radius; returns are refused to the wrong sticker and until Sam's ball is back; only the three honest cards count. Parameterised answers n-k, 2*n, n-k and n-k stay positive at every corner.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the slips named in the adult text: taking without asking (Grab it refusal, p1, m9, challenge 'grab'), believing please obliges a yes (Take it anyway refusal, ask predict, p3, m3, challenge 'nomeans'), keeping it until finished when the owner asks (Sam-first refusal, give-back predict, m1, challenge 'keep'), careless use near mess (book route hazards, carry predict, p5, m4, challenge 'care') and hiding damage or lying (three refused crayon cards, oops predict, m2, challenge 'hide').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagborrow is built around an object that belongs to someone else: the owner's reply decides the outcome, the borrowed book must be steered round juice, paint, a puppy and sand, items carry owner name stickers that decide where they go back, and a snapped crayon tests owning up. flagshare (lesson 357) is about turn order and fair shares of snacks, and lesson 318's choices lab treats right and wrong broadly; neither has the ask-and-accept, care-in-transit or return-to-owner mechanics.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child finds each rule by trying: Grab it is stopped with 'the scooter is Mia's, ask first', Take it anyway after a no says please does not oblige a yes, dragging the book across the room spills juice or paint and sends it back to the start, giving Leo's car to Sam names the sticker, returning anything before Sam's ball says give it when asked, and Hide it explains what Ben would find. Done messages state the rule after the scene has shown it.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions with a tempting wrong option that the lab disproves: 'Yes, because I said please' (Sam and Leo still say not now and no), 'Yes, straight across is fine' (the straight route hits a hazard), 'Keep it until I finish' (other returns are refused until Sam's ball goes back) and 'Put it back so he does not see' (that card is refused with the reason).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions; wrong options carry five tagged messages naming the slip: grab (it belongs to someone else, ask first), nomeans (asking nicely does not mean they must say yes), keep (give it back straight away when asked), care (keep borrowed things clean and give them back to the owner) and hide (hiding or not telling is not fair; tell, say sorry, help put it right).

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short sentences and a named friend (FK -0.9, family kid limit 5); canvas text is a one-line banner, friend names and short two-line cards; the adult text is FK 9.0, under the family adult limit of 10, with EYFS and PSHE terms kept there.

no_filler.evidence: Kid paragraphs: ask first, the owner's choice, gentle hands and giving back, and owning up. Adult paragraphs: EYFS and PSHE placement, the four parts of borrowing, five named mistakes with the advice not to punish honest telling, and what each scene does. The content gate's filler and 12% duplicate checks pass.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px screenshots in light and dark: the friend and toy sit above two 170 px reply pads, the book route has 54 px hazard circles with a clear edge corridor and a 50 px draggable book, the owner and item tiles are about 115 px wide in two rows with readable name stickers, the six crayon cards wrap onto two lines without clipping, and the lend cards fill two columns. The iPhone 13 walkthrough completes every Show me.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: the two replies to each friend, the two routes for the book, Pick the car, ball or book then Give to each friend, one button per crayon card and per lend card. The canvas aria-label reports every refusal and success in words; axe WCAG 2.1 AA runs clean in light and dark themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
